    How I work
  
  
    
    
      My background is mathematics and environmental data science, and I work on forests, fire, and water. I need to know why a thing is being asked before I am much use on how, partly because it changes what I build and partly because it is most of why I want to. The data usually arrives tangled: undocumented, scattered across sources, or answering a question nobody has phrased precisely enough yet. I take it apart until I can see the root, write down what I found, and put it back so it holds up for whoever needs it next. There is more detail in my CV and on the research page.
     
    
  



  I would give my right arm for the simplicity on the far side of complexity.
  Oliver Wendell Holmes

    The duck method
  
  When I was a little girl, I knew another little girl who could draw a duck. I could not draw a duck. She appeared to possess some mysterious duck-drawing faculty that had passed me over. But I had seen proof that a duck could be drawn, so I kept trying. Now I can draw a duck.
  
    
      What the duck?
    
    
      I did not know then that it would keep happening. It starts with someone who can do a thing I cannot, and me thinking it is the best thing ever. Then I am aghast that I have not learned it yet. It is FOMO, but for skills. And so I go learn it, and usually keep going past what I set out for. I do that with most things. I did not stop at ducks; there is a page containing some of what came after.
      This kind of can do attitudeFor a truly tragic lack of a better phrase. works on objects as well as systems. Sometimes the payoff is another ten years with a favorite shirt. Sometimes it is a better pipeline. Both need someone to stop and look before discarding, which the urgency pandemic of modern life trains out of us. That pause is also the subject of one of my poems, Urgency.
